(West Palm Beach, Florida) * [[Forest Hill Community High School|Forest Hill]]
(West Palm Beach, Florida) | college = * [[Independence Community College|Independence CC]] (2020–2021) * [[Northeastern Oklahoma A&M]] (2021–2022) * [[Missouri State Bears basketball|Missouri State]] (2022–2023) * [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco]] (2023–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 31 | draft_team = [[Toronto Raptors]] | career_start = 2024 | years1 = {{nbay|2024|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | years2 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]]–[[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team2 = →[[Raptors 905]] | years3 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team3 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years4 = [[2026–27 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team4 = →[[Stockton Kings]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2024) * WCC Newcomer of the Year (2024) }} '''Jonathan Michael Mogbo''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|oʊ||b|oʊ}} {{respell|MOH-boh}}; born October 29, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Independence Community College|Independence CC Pirates]], the [[Northeastern Oklahoma A&M College|Northeastern Oklahoma A&M Golden Norsemen]], the [[Missouri State Bears basketball|Missouri State Bears]] and the [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco Dons]]. ==Early life and high school career== Mogbo was raised in [[Wellington, Florida]], by his parents Chuck and Karen Mogbo.{{cite web|first=Josh|last=Lewenberg|title=Raptors’ Mogbo fulfils NBA dream after taking unconventional path|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/raptors-mogbo-fulfils-nba-dream-after-taking-unconventional-path-1.2152533|website=TSN.ca|date=July 24, 2024|access-date=December 13, 2024}} His father is of Nigerian descent and his mother is Jamaican. Mogbo has two older stepbrothers and one older brother. Mogbo played [[American football|football]] while growing up and did not start playing organized basketball until he was in the fourth grade. He played alongside future [[Toronto Raptors]] teammate [[Scottie Barnes]] on an [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball team. Barnes lived with Mogbo and his family during his freshman year when they both attended [[Cardinal Newman High School (West Palm Beach, Florida)|Cardinal Newman High School]] in [[West Palm Beach, Florida]]. Mogbo later attended [[Forest Hill Community High School]].{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Nelsen|title=HS boys basketball: Forest Hill puts on a show in win over Hallandale|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2019/11/27/hs-boys-basketball-forest-hill-puts-on-show-in-win-over-hallandale/2203382007/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240530124025/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2019/11/27/hs-boys-basketball-forest-hill-puts-on-show-in-win-over-hallandale/2203382007/|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 30, 2024|work=[[The Palm Beach Post]]|date=November 27, 2019|access-date=May 30, 2024}} ==College career== Mogbo had no Division I scholarship offers in high school and began his college basketball career at [[Independence Community College]].{{cite web|first=Ron|last=Kroichick|title=Jonathan Mogbo flourishes at USF, fifth school in 5 years, 5 states|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/jonathan-mogbo-flourishes-usf-fifth-school-5-18705974.php|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=March 9, 2024|access-date=May 29, 2024}} He transferred to [[Northeastern Oklahoma A&M College]] before the start of his sophomore season.{{cite web|first=Jim|last=Meehan|title=Key matchup: USF's Jonathan Mogbo, Gonzaga's Anton Watson have similar roles|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2024/jan/24/key-matchup-usfs-jonathan-mogbo-gonzagas-anton-wat/|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=January 24, 2024|access-date=May 29, 2024}} Mogbo averaged 14.3 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks per game with the Golden Norsemen.{{cite web|first=Wyatt D.|last=Wheeler|title=Jonathan Mogbo: Missouri State basketball adds juco transfer|url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/college/msu/2022/04/22/jonathan-mogbo-missouri-state-basketball-juco-transfer-dana-ford-northeastern-oklahoma-neo/7412497001/|work=[[Springfield News-Leader]]|date=April 22, 2022|access-date=May 30, 2024}} Mogbo transferred to [[Missouri State Bears basketball|Missouri State]] for his junior season.{{cite web|first=Cole|last=Forsman|title=West Coast Conference transfer portal update: Gonzaga, Santa Clara, LMU reload for 2023-24|url=https://www.si.com/college/gonzaga/basketball/west-coast-conference-transfer-portal-update-gonzaga-santa-clara-lmu-reload-for-2023-24|website=[[SI.com]]|date=August 23, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2024}} He was the Bears' starting power forward and averaged eight points, seven rebounds, 1.4 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.1 blocks per game. After the season, Mogbo entered NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|first=Wyatt D.|last=Wheeler|title=Missouri State basketball starter Jonathan Mogbo enters transfer portal|url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/sports/college/msu/2023/03/14/jonathan-mogbo-transfer-portal-missouri-state-northeastern-oklahoma-am-college-basketaball/70009954007/|work=[[Springfield News-Leader]]|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2024}} Mogbo ultimately transferred to [[San Francisco Dons men's basketball|San Francisco]].{{cite web|first=Connor|last=Letourneau|title=How NIL upends Bay Area schools' basketball recruiting|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/college/article/nil-basketball-bay-area-recruiting-18472265.php|work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]|date=November 24, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2024}}{{cite web|title=USF Adds Dynamic Forward Jonathan Mogbo|url=https://usfdons.com/news/2023/4/25/mens-basketball-usf-adds-dynamic-forward-jonathan-mogbo.aspx|website=USFDons.com|date=April 25, 2023|access-date=May 30, 2024}} He was named the [[West Coast Conference]] (WCC) Newcomer of the Year and first-team All-WCC after averaging 14.2 points and a conference-high 10.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Wilner|title=Gonzaga and Brigham Young will rule the West in men's basketball next season|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/college/gonzaga-and-brigham-young-will-rule-the-west-in-mens-basketball-next-season/|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=April 11, 2024|access-date=May 30, 2024}} After the season, Mogbo declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] and re-entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]]. He opted to remain in the draft and forgo his remaining season of college eligibility.{{cite web|first=Cody|last=Taylor|title=Report: San Francisco junior Jonathan Mogbo to remain in 2024 NBA draft |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2024/05/28/san-francisco-jonathan-mogbo-2024-nba-draft/|work=Rookie Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=May 28, 2024|access-date=May 30, 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors (2024–2026)=== On June 27, 2024, Mogbo was selected with the 31st overall pick by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]{{cite web|first=Brett|last=Siegel|title=Kyle Filipowski to Jazz headlines best picks of 2024 NBA Draft 2nd round|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kyle-filipowski-to-jazz-headlines-best-picks-of-2024-nba-draft-2nd-round|website=ClutchPoints|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}} and on July 4, he signed with them.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN WALTER, MOGBO AND SHEAD|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-walter-mogbo-and-shead|website=NBA.com|date=July 4, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}} During his rookie season, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Raptors 905 Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Raptors-905/41/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 15, 2025}} On April 9, 2025, Mogbo recorded his first career triple-double with 17 points, 11 assists, and 10 rebounds in a 126–96 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web |agency=Canadian Press | title=Raptors rookie Jonathan Mogbo has first triple-double of career at any level | website=Sportsnet.ca | date=2025-04-09 | url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/mogbo-has-first-career-triple-double-as-raptors-dominate-hornets-in-home-finale/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} He made 63 appearances (including 18 starts) for the Raptors during his rookie campaign, averaging 6.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jonathan Mogbo 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5107897/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Mogbo made 40 appearances for the Raptors during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 1.5 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jonathan Mogbo 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5107897/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2026–present)=== On July 3, 2026, Mogbo signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web |title=Kings Sign Adam Flagler To Two-Way Contract |url=
